# CPU reference

`cpu_reference.txt` was captured on 12 October 2026, before extracting the
numerical stages from `src/runtime/simulation.rs` (original runtime at
`17ce85b`). It is a frozen oracle, not output regenerated by the new backend.

`tests/compute_regression.rs` defines three scenarios: local learning, frozen
learning, and learning with active intrinsic capabilities. Each includes
simultaneous signed inputs, synaptic propagation, local maintenance and a live
synapse replacement. The fixture records reports, time, pending-event count,
clock and intrinsic deadlines, all network state, post traces, homeostasis and
the complete observation log. Both default and explicitly selected CpuCompute
must reproduce it exactly.

The Rust Debug representation is a test format, not a public persistence API.
Changes to that representation require a reviewed fixture migration; changes
to numerical behavior require explicit new expectations rather than blindly
regenerating the baseline.

On 9 November 2026 the fixture was extended only with neutral receptor/release/
modulation fields, zero signed learning eligibility and absent STP metadata.
Every historical numerical value remains unchanged; the old fixture was not
regenerated by the new simulation. Hashes and validation are recorded in
[neuromodulation-verification.json](../../docs/neuromodulation-verification.json).

On 25 November 2026 the local learning rules were changed after the formal
verification, and the fixture was migrated with a review of the difference:

* the weight step lands softly at the configured bounds instead of being cut off,
* the rate correction subtracts the expectation of the timing kernel the rule applies,
* the pair window tapers continuously towards its edge,
* the homeostasis response is smoothed at the firing-rate target,
* the competition budget is capped at the capacity of the positive weights.

Only values that depend on these rules differ: weights, transmitted amplitudes,
input traces, membrane potentials and the new homeostasis field. The structure of
the recorded state, the event order and the spike counts are unchanged. The
migration is documented in
[neuromodulation-verification.json](../../docs/neuromodulation-verification.json)
under `rule_change_migration`; the previous and the new hash are recorded there.
The fixture is only rewritten when `NERVA_UPDATE_REFERENCE` is set, so that a
migration stays a deliberate step.
